pairs.evidence: src/lib/db/loop-runs-stale.ts:73 The GET /api/org/loop sweep (route.ts:84) runs this lookup; when it fails, the error becomes an empty exclusion set, so runs driven by remote agents or hosted workers are written `stopped` and their lanes and claims released, which treats a failed probe as proof of death (the comment above even admits a wrongly stopped run is work thrown away).

techniques.evidence: src/lib/db/loop-runs-stale.ts:73 A failed lookup should land on unknown, not dead. Here it falls through to the stop updateMany, so an unobserved external run is killed.

src/lib/db/loop-runs-types.ts:172 The closed vocabulary has no `lost`. The sweep writes `stopped` (loop-runs-stale.ts:80), the same state an operator Stop yields (loop-engine.ts:967), and the two differ only in free-text error.
src/lib/local/boot-sweep.ts:78 A boot sweep from instrumentation register() reconciles running rows, then removes stranded worktrees, before the first request. The DB row is the source of truth.
src/app/api/org/loop/route.ts:84 A tier-two sweep on read, with the process-wide live predicate, so the run being rendered is not reaped.

src/lib/local/loop-engine.ts:805 Bounded pool under LOOP_CONCURRENCY_CAP (A/B and compare refused past the cap at 295/305), one worktree per repo/arm (809), and a whole-run hosted reservation (537) as the run-total number.
src/lib/local/loop-worktree.ts:263 The stranded-worktree sweep deletes only dirs it can identify as its own temp checkouts, and skips the repo when the listing fails (260).
src/lib/local/loop-engine.ts:688 A retry gets a fresh worktree and branch rather than an unexplained leftover of the previous attempt.
src/lib/local/loop-engine.ts:386 Remote and hosted lanes are rows in `curating` that external workers claim into. The control plane opens no worktree and pushes nothing to them.
src/lib/local/loop-engine.ts:802 On the loop path, a lane's outcome is adjudicated by the parent's rescan of its own worktree, not by the session's report.
